chunk_findings.detail: The hook advice now prints a JSON array as the value of `--add-globs`, but the same change still documents the CLI value as comma-separated in `ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py` (`--add-globs <comma,separated>`), and the diff contains no parser change making `--add-globs` JSON-aware. For staged paths `src/a.py` and `src/b.py`, the refusal prints `ddflow update <ID> --add-globs '["src/a.py", "src/b.py"]'`. If the option is parsed by the comma-separated notation the helper itself names (`globspec.parse`), that value is split into `["src/a.py"` and `"src/b.py"]` (or treated as one JSON-looking glob), neither of which matches the staged paths, so the commit is still refused. The earlier finding is not answered: the printed advice contradicts the only CLI guidance changed here.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:_add_globs_arg

chunk_findings.detail: The helper inserts literal staged paths directly as glob patterns without escaping glob metacharacters. For a staged file named `src/a[b].py`, it emits `--add-globs '["src/a[b].py"]'`; under standard glob semantics `[b]` is a character class, so the added glob matches `src/ab.py`, not the literal path, leaving the commit refused. For a staged file named `src/*.py`, it emits the glob `src/*.py`, which also matches every `.py` file under `src/`, unintentionally widening the lease beyond the staged path.

chunk_findings.detail: The new test pins the hook advice to a JSON array value for `--add-globs`: `ddflow update <ID> --add-globs '["src/a.py", "src/b.py"]'`. The `--add-globs` CLI surface advertised by `ddflow/surfaces/declared/lifecycle_cli.py` is comma-separated, and this manifest only changes the advice/claim text, not the argument parser to accept JSON. If an agent runs the advised command for staged `src/a.py` and `src/b.py`, the parser receives a single JSON-array-looking argument (or comma-splits it into malformed pieces such as `["src/a.py"` and ` "src/b.py"]`), so neither staged path is covered; the commit is refused again. The added test does not answer the earlier finding; it enforces the wrong syntax.

chunk_findings.detail: The advice inserts staged paths directly as glob patterns without escaping glob metacharacters. For a staged literal path `src/a[b].py`, the advised glob `src/a[b].py` uses standard glob semantics where `[b]` matches the single character `b`, so it matches `src/ab.py` but not the staged file, leaving the commit still refused. Conversely, a literal staged path containing `*`, such as `src/*.py`, would be advised as a pattern matching all `.py` files, unintentionally widening the lease. The new comma/apostrophe test only checks shell quoting, not glob escaping, so the earlier glob-metacharacter issue still holds.
